# Milo — full documentation

Documentation from the main branch. The pinned release may not include every feature described here.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/README.md

## Install

The v0.1.4 release is available for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or later. Install it with Homebrew:

```sh
brew install mcc0x/milo/milo
```

Without Homebrew, download and run the installer from the release tag:

```sh
curl -fsSLo milo-install.sh https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/releases/download/v0.1.4/install.sh &&
  sh milo-install.sh
```

The script verifies the release binary against its SHA-256 checksum and installs it to `~/.local/bin` by default. It does not need Rust or Git. See [setup and removal](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md) for source installation and uninstall instructions.

Run `milo` inside Rex to choose your panes and save your workspace preferences.

## Workspace settings

Choose a tree or a project sidebar, try it in this tab, then save it globally or just for this Git worktree. Drag a divider in an installed Milo sidebar and Milo remembers the proportions for that worktree. With **Arrange new shell tabs** enabled, the next shell tab restores them; command tabs and existing layouts are left alone. With **Title Rex tabs** enabled, tabs you have not named show their project, worktree and agent.

Prefer a browser? Run `milo web` in your project. It opens the [local settings editor](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#browser-editor) built into the CLI. It shares settings with `milo setup`; no account or separate install is needed.

<p align="center"><img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/web-settings.webp" width="760" alt="Milo’s browser editor with Outline, History and Usage in order, a left rail at 20% width, and a two-row Usage pane"></p>

## Outline

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/outline.png" width="570" alt="Project files with colours and line counts for changes to commit or push">
</p>

See changed files in the project tree as you work. Bold colours mark changes to commit; regular colours mark changes to push. Press `Enter` on a file to read it.

## History

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/history.png" width="570" alt="Recent commits, with the newest commit open to show its changed files">
</p>

See recent commits and, when the branch tracks a remote branch, how many still need to be pushed. Press `Enter` on a commit to see the files it touched, then on a file to read that version.

## Usage

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/usage.png" width="860" alt="Codex and Claude Code limits showing percent left, time until reset and an Opus weekly limit">
</p>

See how much of each reported limit you have left. Milo reads local reports saved by oh-my-pi, Codex and Claude Code, and the tokens and estimated cost OpenCode recorded today. It shows the tools that have a figure on this Mac, so there is no empty place for one you do not use, and setup can always show or hide each tool. Where the terminal can show pictures, such as in Rex, the pane can draw the logos and large figures as pictures.

### In the macOS menu bar

Keep an eye on usage without switching to Rex. **Milo** shows the mascot beside your lowest fresh remaining percentage. Click it for reset times, or choose **Browser settings…** to open the browser editor.

<p align="center"><img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/menu-bar.webp" width="312" alt="Milo’s macOS menu showing example Codex and Claude Code limits, reset times and a Settings button"></p>

On an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 13 or later, run `milo menubar install`. The Homebrew and release binaries include the app; it only runs if you install it. See [menu bar setup and removal](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#macos-menu-bar).

## Discord presence

Optionally show **In a Rex session** on your Discord profile, under Milo's name and icon, while a Rex app has a session open. It is off until you turn it on with `milo presence enable`, in Settings or in the browser editor, and each of them says what becomes public first. Nothing about your sessions, projects, files or commands is sent unless you also choose to show the name of the session in front, its Git project's folder name, or both. No bot, token or sign-in is involved, and you can use a Discord application of your own instead of Milo's. See [Discord presence](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md) for setup, privacy and limits.

## Reader

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/reader.png" width="675" alt="A TypeScript file with coloured code and green and red lines showing edits">
</p>

Read a file with added and removed lines marked, or open it as it was at a commit. Press `n` or `N` to jump between changed blocks. The reader colours [about thirty languages](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#languages), from Rust and TypeScript to Markdown, HTML and CSS.

Press `e` to edit a working text file where you are reading it. The edit is a draft until you save with `Ctrl-S`, and a save never replaces a file that changed on disk without asking. `Ctrl-F` formats the draft with a [formatter you have installed](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#formatting); `Ctrl-Z` takes it back. See [editing files](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#editing-files).

## Commands

| Command | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `milo` | Milo Home: Browser settings, Terminal settings, Doctor and Uninstall |
| `milo outline [PATH]` | File tree |
| `milo history [PATH]` | Recent commits |
| `milo usage` | Usage limits |
| `milo view FILE [--commit ID \| --edit]` | File reader, or its editor with `--edit` |
| `milo setup` | Setup screen |
| `milo web [--port PORT] [--no-open]` | [Local browser settings editor](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#browser-editor) |
| `milo menubar install` / `uninstall` | Install or remove the optional menu app (menu-enabled builds only) |
| `milo doctor` | Read-only preference and integration report |
| `milo alerts` | [Mirror Rex alerts](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#mirror-rex-alerts) to a Telegram chat or Discord channel; off until you turn it on |
| `milo presence [status]` / `enable` / `details` / `application` / `disable` | Show or change the optional [Discord presence](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md) |

`milo PATH` opens Outline at that path. On a fresh install, `milo` and `milo setup` share a short welcome guide. For unattended installs, `milo setup --skip-onboarding` dismisses it and exits without opening a TUI or applying settings. Direct pane commands never start the guide.

# Set up milo

![Milo’s layout picker with the project sidebar selected beside its split preview](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/setup.png)

## Install

The v0.1.4 prebuilt release is for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or later. Use Homebrew:

```sh
brew install mcc0x/milo/milo
```

Or download the versioned release installer from GitHub:

```sh
curl -fsSLo milo-install.sh https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/releases/download/v0.1.4/install.sh &&
  sh milo-install.sh
```

The installer checks the binary against a pinned SHA-256 checksum before placing it in `~/.local/bin`. Set `MILO_BIN_DIR` to choose a different directory. The prebuilt installer does not need a compiler, Cargo or Git.

To build from source instead, install Git and Rust 1.91 or later, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mcc0x/milo.git
cd milo
sh install.sh
```

The source installer builds the checkout containing the script, even when launched from another directory. A standalone or piped copy clones Milo from GitHub into a private temporary directory instead.

The source installer also honours `MILO_BIN_DIR` and defaults to `~/.local/bin`.

Current installers write a receipt for the binary and its install path. Use a current installer with `--uninstall` and the same `MILO_BIN_DIR` to remove it. If the binary has changed or the receipt is missing or invalid, the installer leaves the binary in place. Older installs may not have a receipt; verify the binary before removing it manually rather than running an older installer’s `--uninstall`.

## In Rex

In a Rex shell run `milo setup`. Pick **Just the tree**, **Project sidebar**, or start from the tab you already arranged. Adjust the individual panes and appearance if needed. Trying the layout does not change your saved default; undo the trial before saving if it isn't what you want.

In Home, the welcome guide and Settings, moving the pointer over a clickable control underlines it without changing your keyboard selection. **Click once** to open a menu, switch sections or change a value. Click **Save** and choose a scope to keep your changes. Terminals without mouse-motion reporting still support the arrow keys and Enter.

In narrow Settings panes, rows use shorter labels. When there's room, the full name and value of the selected setting appear below the list.

**Unsaved changes** stays visible while you edit. If you leave Settings from Home or `milo setup`, choose **Save**, **Discard**, or **Keep editing**. Save asks for a scope for each changed group: layout, then appearance and workflow together. Claude Code choices apply to the active profile and do not need a scope. Each confirmed save takes effect as you go, so going back does not undo changes you have already saved. Leaving also undoes any layout trial you haven't kept by saving it.

Save for **this worktree** to keep a project-specific setup, or save a **global default** for projects without an override. Worktrees of the same repository can have different choices. Preferences live on the machine running Milo, outside the repository. A project cannot install actions or supply a command for Milo to execute.

If the saved layout changes while Settings is open, Milo keeps the newer layout instead of overwriting it. Reopen Settings to edit that layout.

Saving appearance or workflow preferences changes only the settings you edited. A worktree still inherits global values for any settings it does not override, and saving global defaults does not copy worktree overrides.

If a worktree's preferences file is unreadable or invalid, panes keep using global preferences. If the global file is broken, panes use built-in defaults. Milo leaves the files alone and shows a notice; run `milo doctor` to find the file and the error, then correct it and reopen the panes.

Usage starts as a two-row strip in the shared sidebar. Drag a divider in an installed Milo sidebar and Milo remembers the proportions for that Git worktree automatically. To save a layout explicitly or make it the global default, use **Milo: Remember This Layout…**. Milo stores pane roles and proportions, not processes or live pane IDs. Mixed rails containing another app are left alone.

![A Rex tab with Outline, History and the compact Usage readout in one rail beside the shell](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/tab.png)

Turn on **Arrange new shell tabs** to apply the layout to new shell tabs, including the first tab of a new session. Save this switch globally; changing it alone does not replace either the global or worktree layout. If Usage is sized in rows, Milo waits for a Rex client to measure the tab, so a background tab may arrange when you first show it. Tabs opened to run a command and tabs with their own layout are left alone. Turn it off and save globally to stop arranging new tabs. The panes also work on their own outside Rex.

Use the appearance choices to preview icons, choose text change marks, and turn animated activity marks off. Usage shows Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode only while each has a figure to show; choose **Always show** or **Hide** for a tool to [decide that yourself](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#which-tools-appear). Use the workflow choices to pin Outline and History to the starting project or follow the shell they were opened beside. Milo does not change Rex's font, theme, shortcuts or notification settings.

**After Rex restarts, a sidebar can come back as shells instead of Milo.** The dividers and pane labels survive, but on Rex preview.21 (server API 18) the running programs do not. To restore the sidebar, focus its tab’s working shell and run **Milo: Arrange This Tab** in the Rex app. Milo checks what’s running before it offers to rebuild. New shell tabs are arranged as before.

**Text zoom is separate from split size.** On Rex preview.21 (server API 18), Milo can read a terminal's cell dimensions, but creating or resizing a terminal does not set the font the Mac app renders. The app exposes relative font actions and an app-wide [starting font size](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/reference/mac-settings.md#setting-typography-font-size), not an absolute per-pane zoom setting. Milo therefore remembers divider positions, not text zoom, for Outline, History and Usage.

Run `milo` for Home or `milo setup` to go directly to Settings. Both share the same first-run guide. To skip it in an install script, run `milo setup --skip-onboarding`; it records the skip and exits without requiring a terminal or installing integrations. `milo outline` and the other direct pane commands never show the guide. Terminal panes work without Rex; split geometry and shell-following require Rex.

## Tab titles and session names

Milo leaves tab and session names alone unless you ask. It builds a name from folder names and the name of an agent's process. It never reads what a terminal shows, a terminal's title or a program's status text, so nothing you type to an agent ends up in a name.

Turn on **Title Rex tabs** under **Workflow** in terminal Settings or **Integrations → Rex automation** in the browser to name tabs that nobody has named. A tab is titled after the Git project its shell is in: `project` in the repository's own folder and `project/worktree` in a linked worktree. While Claude Code, Codex or oh-my-pi runs in one of the tab's shells, the title ends with ` · claude`, ` · codex` or ` · omp`. A tab outside a Git project keeps the label Rex gave it. The setting is off by default. Save it globally, or for one worktree to title tabs only there or everywhere but there.

Milo titles a tab only while its label is Rex's own, such as `Window 89abcdef`, or the title Milo set last. Rename a tab yourself, in the app or with `rex window rename`, and Milo stops titling it. Clear the name to hand the tab back. Milo remembers the titles it set by Rex window ID in its state folder, so a name you chose is still respected after Rex or Milo's listener restarts.

New tabs use the current title setting. For an open tab with file-backed preferences, the listener picks up an edit on the next shell or tab-layout event, without polling. Otherwise the title is reconsidered when the directory or foreground agent changes. Turning titles off returns the tab to Rex's label. Agents are recognised by their program name: one started under another name, such as `node`, is not shown.

The listener starts Milo to ask about a directory once, and with titles on once more for each agent that runs there. After that it asks again when your global preferences or that worktree's own have changed, or when a folder outside any project has gained a repository. So with titles off, other tabs in a directory and later visits to it normally start no further process. Milo is asked every time about a directory it cannot vouch for: one outside a project with a folder above it that other users can write to, such as `/tmp`, one reached through a link, or one where Git could not run.

**Milo: Name Session from This Project** renames the session you run it in after the project of its shell: `project`, or `project/worktree` in a linked worktree, without the agent. It is the only way Milo names a session, and it happens only when you run the action: from the command palette, with a key you bound to it, or with `rex do milo_name_session`. It creates no session and switches to none. Outside a Git project it changes nothing and says so. Milo does not remember the name or keep it up to date, so rename the session again whenever you like. The action does not depend on **Title Rex tabs**.

Both need the installed Rex integration. After upgrading Milo, run `milo setup --repair` so Rex loads the current actions and listener.

## Browser editor

Run `milo web` from the project you want to configure, or choose **Browser settings** from Milo Home. Milo opens the editor through a short-lived private file so it doesn’t pass the session key to the launcher. If the editor doesn’t open, use the private link printed in the terminal. `milo web --no-open` prints that link without opening a browser. Keep the command running while you edit. The page is served by the Milo executable on this machine, not by usemilo.net. No account, network service, or separate frontend install is needed. Don’t share the link.

![The local editor showing pane order, rail side, width and Usage height for an example worktree](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/web-settings.webp)

On macOS, the optional [Milo menu app](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#macos-menu-bar) also opens this editor from **Browser settings…**. To configure a particular worktree, run `milo web` from that project.

The editor listens on `127.0.0.1:6110` by default. Use `milo web --port 7000` to choose another port, or `--port 0` for an available port when running a second editor.

Use **Layout** for pane order and sizes, **Panes** for Outline, History and shared appearance, and **Usage** for tools, accounts and display. In Rex, the layout actions menu lets you copy the current tab’s layout or try the draft in that tab. Undo a trial to restore the previous layout. Save explicitly for the current worktree or as the global default; Claude Code choices apply to the active profile. Outside Rex you can still edit and save settings.

**Integrations** groups Rex automation, Discord presence and alert forwarding. Rex automation uses drafts; presence and forwarding apply immediately. **Menu Bar** manages the optional macOS app, and **Health** checks for problems.

After saving, the confirmation names the destination: global defaults, the current worktree, or the active Claude profile. If open panes still use the old preferences, the browser keeps **Reopen panes to apply** in the project bar after the confirmation fades. Editing again clears the reminder.

Terminal Settings and the browser editor check for intervening changes before saving preferences or removing a worktree override. If another editor saved first, reopen the settings and review the current values rather than overwriting them. In terminal Settings, save or discard layout and Claude drafts before repairing or removing integrations.

In **Health**, run a check of saved settings and the live layout. If the original Rex tab is no longer available, Health warns unless it finds a more serious issue. Saving settings or changing the live layout clears the old result; run the check again for an updated verdict.

While the page is open, it periodically keeps the local session alive only if it has unsaved changes, an active layout trial, or queued edits. This does not save your work, and the session can still time out if the browser suspends the page.

**Done** closes the editor only after undoing any active layout trial. If undo fails, the editor stays open so you can retry. Stopping Milo with `Ctrl-C` or letting it time out only attempts to undo the trial. Closing the browser tab alone leaves the private link usable until Milo stops or the session is idle for 15 minutes. When the session ends, unsaved drafts are discarded; saved settings stay as they are.

The dashboard ships inside `milo`: using it needs no Node runtime, account, or internet connection. For UI development, use Node 26 and Bun: `cd dashboard && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run dev`. Open the private URL printed in the terminal. Next.js Fast Refresh updates the interface against a real local Milo session. `MILO_BIN` selects the backend executable (default `milo` on PATH); `MILO_PROJECT` selects the project to edit; `PORT` selects the development port (default `6110`). Stop the development server with `Ctrl-C`.

## Rex actions

Saving installs these actions in the Rex command palette:

| Action | Name for a key binding |
| --- | --- |
| Milo: Arrange This Tab | `milo_layout` |
| Milo: Add the Outline | `milo_outline` |
| Milo: Add the History | `milo_history` |
| Milo: Add the Usage | `milo_usage` |
| Milo: Close Panes in This Tab | `milo_close` |
| Milo: Peek Outline | `milo_peek_outline` |
| Close the outline peek | `milo_close_peek` |
| Remember the current rail | `milo_remember_layout` |
| Reset a remembered layout | `milo_reset_layout` |
| Name the session after this project | `milo_name_session` |

Milo does not install key bindings. For an optional shortcut, check Rex's shortcut settings and `rex keymap` first; the latter lists config bindings, not every Mac app shortcut. If the chord is free, put a binding such as `rex.bind("cmd+shift+m", "milo_peek_outline")` in your own Rex `init.lua`. Actions also work directly in the palette without any binding.

Peek opens a floating outline and takes focus. Invoking it again raises the same peek. Dismiss it to return to the originating pane. Adding the docked Outline instead keeps the shell focused. Your existing custom actions remain yours.

Setup adds two marked lines at the top of `~/.config/rex/init.lua` (after the interpreter line, if it has one) and asks Rex to reload. The actions live in `~/.config/milo/rex.lua`. `~/.config/milo/listener.lua` watches for divider changes even when arranging new shell tabs is off, and titles tabs when you have chosen that. If `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is an absolute path, both folders live there instead. `$REX_CONFIG` can point directly to a different settings file. Milo keeps its saved state in `~/.local/state/milo` or under an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME`.

Setup does not rewrite your actions or key bindings. It refuses to change read-only settings files or use a linked milo configuration folder. The settings file itself may be a symbolic link: setup edits the target and keeps the link.

## Claude Code limits

**Show Claude Code limits** adds milo to `~/.claude/settings.json` only if you do not already have a status line. Turning it off removes milo's entry, not one you added yourself. If the option is unavailable because you already have a status line, milo leaves it alone; [other sources](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#where-the-figures-come-from) may already provide limits.

If you set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, Milo uses that profile's `settings.json` instead and tracks its installation separately.

New setups use the full path to Milo, so Claude Code does not need `milo` on its `PATH`. If Doctor reports an old launcher, turn limits off, save, then turn them back on and save.

## Mirror Rex alerts

Milo can send the same Rex alert to Telegram, Discord, or both. Forwarding is off until you enable it. Rex's own tab marks, sounds and notifications stay as they are: Milo listens to `rex events` and changes no Rex setting.

```sh
milo alerts telegram -1001234567890   # asks for the bot's token; or: milo alerts discord
milo alerts                           # what is saved, whether it is running, what would be sent
milo alerts test                      # one message written by Milo
milo alerts on                        # starts, and says again what is sent
milo alerts on discord                # enable just Discord, leaving Telegram as configured
milo alerts on telegram               # now send to both
milo alerts test telegram             # test only Telegram
milo alerts off                       # ends it at once
```

The same choices are under **Integrations → Alert forwarding** in `milo web`, and under **Workflow → Mirror Rex alerts…** in `milo setup`; both say what will be sent and ask before turning it on. The setup screen switches between saved destinations but never takes a secret: save one with `milo alerts` or the browser editor.

In the browser, choose **Set up destination** (or **Manage destinations**). For Telegram, enter the bot token and look for a chat in its recent updates. If your chat isn’t listed, message the bot there and try again, or enter the chat ID or public `@channel` yourself. Bots already using a webhook need manual entry; Milo doesn’t disconnect their webhook. Looking for chats doesn’t save a destination or turn on forwarding.

Each saved destination has its own forwarding switch and test button. Turn on both switches to send each alert to both places, or test either destination without enabling forwarding. Forgetting one leaves the other connected.

Changing the recipient or replacing its credential turns off forwarding to that provider until you approve it again. Re-saving identical manual credentials leaves forwarding unchanged. If another editor changes what will be sent while confirmation is open, review the updated details. An old preview Telegram credential without a verifiable chat identity must be paired again; Milo will not guess which DM it belongs to.

**Connect with Milo (requires the hosted service).** The official endpoint is `https://connect.usemilo.net`; the settings dashboard still runs on your device. If the service is not available, use manual setup. For Telegram, confirm in a private DM with Milo’s bot. For Discord, authorize a webhook for your channel. Copy the finish code from the bot’s reply or the confirmation page, then paste it **only in the Milo dashboard where you started pairing**. Pasting or selecting browser autofill opens the destination review. If you type the code, choose **Check connection**. Never send the code to someone who shared a pairing link. The destination is saved only when you choose **Save**; forwarding is enabled separately.

Telegram alerts use the relay; Discord alerts go directly from your device to your channel. Manual setup works without the hosted service. For local development or deployment requirements, see the [relay guide](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/hosted/README.md).

<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/web-alerts-mobile.webp">
  <img src="https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/web-alerts.webp" width="760" alt="The Alerts page of the browser editor: mirroring is off, alerts would go to an example Telegram channel, and the page says that only the kind of alert and the program's short name are sent">
</picture>

![The setup screen's Mirror Rex alerts panel: mirroring off, Telegram as destination, the three status alerts on, notifications and bells off, and Kind only as what is sent](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/setup-alerts.webp)

**What counts as an alert.** A program that reports through Rex's [program status protocol](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status) that it is `blocked`, failed (`error`) or finished (`done`); a program that asks for a desktop notification (OSC 9 or OSC 777); and the terminal bell. The first three are mirrored unless you choose otherwise with `milo alerts events blocked,error,done,notification,bell`. Working and idle reports, progress, exits, titles and everything else in a session are never sent, and neither is anything Milo itself shows.

**What is sent.** By default only the kind of alert and the program's short name, such as `Rex: claude-code is waiting for permission`: no text from the program and no session, tab, folder or file name. `milo alerts content text` adds up to 300 characters of the line the program gave Rex, which can name files or quote a prompt. Both the name and that line come from the program, so they are sent marked as code, where neither Telegram nor Discord makes a link, a mention or formatting of them. The line is also cut to one line with every `@` broken, Discord is told to notify no user, role or `@everyone`, and link previews are turned off.

Discord sends one Milo card per alert, with the Milo icon beside the status, inline code for program names and optional text, a localized send time, and a colored edge: amber for attention, red for errors, green for completion, and Milo blue for notifications, bells and connection tests. Telegram keeps its compact text format.

**Destinations and secrets.** For Telegram, create a bot with BotFather, add it to the chat or channel, and give Milo the chat's number or a public channel's `@name`. For Discord, create a webhook in the channel's **Integrations** settings and give Milo its link; only `discord.com` webhook links are accepted. The bot token or webhook link is asked for without being shown, or read from standard input, never taken as an argument. On macOS it is kept in your Keychain; elsewhere in `alerts-secrets` in Milo's state folder, readable only by you. Settings pages show whether a secret is saved, never the secret. Saving a second destination while alerts are being mirrored does not move them: switch with `milo alerts use`. `milo alerts forget telegram` or `forget discord` removes one, and `milo setup --remove` removes both and ends mirroring.

**Once, not twice.** One background process mirrors, whatever number of tabs, panes and Rex apps are open. Rex repeats a status each time a program reports it; Milo sends it when a terminal enters a state or changes what it is waiting for. A terminal's bell is sent at most once in 30 seconds, and so is a notification that repeats that terminal's last one.

**When things go wrong.** Messages are spaced about a second apart and limited to 20 a minute; a burst beyond that is not sent, and the next message says how many were left out. If the destination asks Milo to slow down, Milo sends nothing until the time it gives has passed, and tries the waiting alert again if that is within a minute. An unreachable or failing destination is tried three times before the alert is dropped. If the destination refuses the secret, or turns down five messages in a row, Milo stops asking until you save the destination again, change a choice or run `milo alerts on`. `milo alerts` shows the last outcome.

**Limits.** Mirroring needs `/usr/bin/curl`, and follows the Rex server on this machine only. It starts with `milo alerts on`, and again whenever Rex starts Milo's listener, which Rex does each time its server loads a [saved layout](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#in-rex); without a saved layout, run `milo alerts on` after restarting the machine. Alerts raised while Rex or the mirroring process is not running are not sent later, because Rex does not replay events. Rex decides in each app whether to show its own notification (for example only in the background, or not for a muted tab) and does not report that decision, so Milo mirrors what programs reported, not what Rex showed. A terminal's notifications through OSC 99 do not appear in Rex's event stream and are not mirrored.

## Remove milo

The menu app and CLI uninstall separately. If you want both gone, run `milo menubar uninstall` **before** removing the CLI. This stops the app and unregisters launch at login. Skip this step if you want to keep using the menu bar.

If [Discord presence](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md) is on, **Uninstall Milo** in Home turns it off and takes the activity down. Before removing the binary any other way, run `milo presence disable`.

From Home, choose **Uninstall Milo** to review and confirm removal of the CLI and its managed integrations. **Health → Remove integration** and `milo setup --remove` only disconnect the managed integrations; they do not remove the executable. For manual removal:

1. To diagnose a setup before changing it, run `milo doctor`. To fix the managed integration after an upgrade or executable move, run `milo setup --repair` with the binary you intend to keep.
2. Before deleting the binary, run `milo setup --remove` to disconnect the managed Rex and Claude Code integrations. It also ends [alert mirroring](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#mirror-rex-alerts) and removes its saved destinations and secrets. Saved preferences and user-edited files are not an uninstall target. Close any live Milo panes separately.
3. Remove the binary with `brew uninstall milo` if you installed with Homebrew. If you used the release installer, run `sh milo-install.sh --uninstall` with your downloaded copy. If you built from source, run `sh install.sh --uninstall` from the checkout. For either script, use the same `MILO_BIN_DIR` you installed to if you set one. Removing the binary does not change Rex or Claude Code settings or remove milo's saved state.

If Rex cannot reload during removal, Milo still removes the managed files and tells you to restart Rex. If Milo cannot safely remove its Claude Code status line, correct the reported settings problem and retry before deleting the executable.

If you set `XDG_STATE_HOME` when installing the integration, use the same value for repair and removal. Milo won’t guess which listener or Claude settings entry belongs to an installation it can’t verify.

`milo setup --remove` disconnects only the active Claude Code profile. Before removing the binary, repeat it for any alternate profiles where you enabled limits, using the same `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` as when you enabled them.

## Troubleshooting

Choose **Doctor** in Home or **Read diagnostics** in Settings to check the installation. Press `Esc` to go back without waiting for the checks to finish. For a report to copy from the shell, run `milo doctor`.

- **`milo` is not found:** for Homebrew, check that Homebrew is on `PATH`. The scripts put milo in `~/.local/bin` unless you set `MILO_BIN_DIR`. Add the install directory to `PATH`, or run the binary by its full path.
- **Doctor reports a Rex loader conflict, or setup says Milo's Rex lines were moved, copied or changed:** Milo leaves your Rex settings and listener alone. In the Rex settings file named by Doctor, restore a single copy of Milo's original two lines at the top, just after any interpreter line. Then run Doctor again.
- **Doctor reports an unreadable saved layout profile:** restore a known-good copy of the named file, or back it up and move it aside. Then reopen Settings to use the fallback layout or save a new one. Integration repair does not replace layout profiles.
- **A save was interrupted or actions are missing:** run `milo doctor`. It checks the managed `rex.lua` and `listener.lua` on disk separately from the actions Rex has loaded. If it reports an out-of-date managed file, a stale launcher, a pending reload or missing managed actions, run `milo setup --repair` with the binary you intend Rex to use. If Doctor identifies a custom file, review it yourself. The **Health** section in setup offers the same diagnostics, repair and removal.
- **The sidebar opens at a different size:** run `milo doctor` from that Rex tab to compare the saved sidebar width and Usage height with what's live. If the sizes differ, check [Autobalance splits](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/reference/mac-settings.md#setting-splits-focus-autobalance-splits) under **Settings → Interface → Splits & Focus**. If it is on, turn it off, then close and re-add the Milo panes to apply the saved sizes.
- **Another setup is saving:** only one setup can save at a time. Wait for it to finish before retrying.
- **New shell tabs are not arranged:** enable **Arrange new shell tabs** under **Customize panes**, then save globally. The listener is an account setting, not a per-project switch. `milo doctor` checks whether it is actually running.
- **After Rex restarts, the sidebar shows shell prompts:** Doctor can identify when the sidebar contains restored shells. Finish any work in them and run **Milo: Arrange This Tab**. When Milo can verify the shells are idle, **Keep shells** leaves them untouched; confirming **Rebuild sidebar** closes them, discards their input and scrollback, and opens Milo’s panes with the worktree’s layout. Milo won’t type into a shell or automatically rebuild on restart. If it can’t verify the panes or show a confirmation, inspect them yourself, close only shells you no longer need, and run Arrange again.
- **A tab is not titled:** `milo doctor` shows whether **Rex tab titles** is on for this worktree and whether the listener is running. The listener runs while the saved layout has at least one pane or arranges new tabs. A tab with a name of its own is left alone: clear the name in Rex to let Milo title it. For an already-open tab, change shell directories to trigger a fresh title check.
- **Icons appear as boxes:** choose plain symbols or no icons in setup, or override one launch with `MILO_ICONS=plain` or `MILO_ICONS=off`. Choose a Nerd Font in Rex only if you want one for all of your terminals.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md

# Using the panes

Run the panes in a Unix terminal with 256 colours. Outline and history start in the current directory unless you give them a path. Inside a Git repository they use its root, even when you start in a subfolder. In a plain folder, outline shows just the files and history says it is not a Git project. To outline a directory named like a command, give its path explicitly: `milo ./history`.

If you initialize Git in that folder, open panes pick up the repository and its saved worktree choices without restarting. Switching branches does not erase remembered folder folds or mark the newly visible timeline as newly arrived.

In Follow mode, Outline and History use the local shell's working directory, even with a coding agent in the foreground and no directory report from the prompt. If the directory is missing, the pane says **Waiting for shell**; if it cannot open the reported folder, it says **Shell folder unavailable**. It keeps showing the last project and names it when space permits. Neither message changes your project preference to Pin.
If shell tracking itself stops, the notice changes to **Shell tracking unavailable**. Reopen the pane to reconnect.

## What fits in a pane

| Pane | Size | What you see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outline | 7 rows or fewer | A strip of changed files in a Git project, most recently written first, flowed across the width |
| Outline | 52 columns or more | In the tree, the type of change and how many lines each file gained and lost |
| Outline and history | 12 rows or more | A key hint |
| History | 3 rows or fewer | Recent commits without the heading, dots or divider |
| History | 52 columns and 8 rows or more | A row of dots when there is more than one commit |
| History | Narrow | A shorter summary, such as `↑2` for two commits to push or `no tracking` for a branch that does not track a remote branch |
| History | Narrow and focused | The selected commit's subject wraps so you can read it without widening the rail |
| Usage | Narrow | The limiting window takes priority; if its status does not fit, the provider name stays visible |
| Reader | 2 rows | The filename and one line of content; `n` and `N` show the changed line itself |

In narrow History, the wrapped subject uses only the room below a clicked row, so the row stays under the pointer. In a two-row pane, expanding a commit uses the second row for its first file or an empty-commit note. Collapse it to see the subject again.

The outline and history update on their own. macOS uses file-change notifications. Where the pane needs to watch but notifications are missing, including on Linux, milo checks about every two seconds. See [keys and marks](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md) for colours and symbols.

In a plain folder, Outline lists the top level and the folders you expand. A partial-listing warning means Milo reached the 50,000-entry limit or couldn't read every entry. In both plain folders and Git worktrees, Outline warns and omits names that aren't valid UTF-8 rather than showing a name that could open a different file.

If Git holds the index lock for more than a moment, Outline, History and the working-file Reader show `Waiting for Git` and pause automatic updates. They update when the lock clears; Milo never removes it.

Untracked files appear before Milo counts their lines. In a wide outline, `?` means the count is not ready, not zero. The outline counts the files in view in small batches as you scroll; a folder shows `?` while any of its new files are still uncounted.

If filtering or folding hides the selected file, Outline keeps the cursor on its nearest visible folder. Press `r` to refresh counts, including offscreen files.

## Comparing commits

History counts commits to push against the branch's tracked remote branch. `no branch tracked` means there is no tracked branch, not that all commits have been pushed. Milo can still use the remote's default branch to mark commits for comparison. `no remote` means the project has no remote configured.

Expand a commit to see its seven-character ID beside the file count. Narrow panes keep that space for the subject instead.

History lists the latest 300 commits. If there are older ones, `G` takes you to the oldest displayed commit, with `Older commits not shown.` underneath when there is room.

A shallow clone has only part of the project's history. If you expand a commit whose parent is beyond the shallow boundary, History says `Shallow history: parent unavailable.` It does not show every file as new. After fetching more history, press `r` to reload. A genuine first commit still shows its added files.

## Reading files

Open a file from the outline or history with `Enter` or a double-click. Inside Rex it opens in a floating reader. Opening another file from that pane replaces only its previous reader, even after following the shell to another project. Any shell you split beside the reader stays open. Outside Rex the reader takes over the pane; `q` brings you back.
History catches up with repository changes when you return from a file, keeping that file selected if it is still in the timeline.

On iPhone, enable [Rex → Settings → Keyboard → Open Keyboard Manually](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/reference/ios-settings#setting-keyboard-open-keyboard-manually) to browse without raising the keyboard. Tap a folder to expand it, tap a file to select it, and double-tap to open it. This setting affects **all** terminal panes on that iPhone, not just Outline. Tap the keyboard button to type in a shell. If the keyboard reopens when you return to a terminal, turn off **Keep Keyboard Open** in the same settings.

For a quick look at the tree, use **Milo: Peek Outline** in Rex. It reuses one floating outline per tab. Close the peek with `Esc` or `q` rather than removing a permanent pane.

`milo view FILE` reads a working file. `milo view FILE --commit ID` reads the version from a commit. Give the file's path as it was in that commit, relative to your current directory or as an absolute path. For example, from `src`, use `milo view main.rs --commit ID`. Milo ignores `.` components and repeated slashes, but rejects `..`. Use a full or abbreviated hexadecimal commit ID, not a branch name or `HEAD`.

Committed-file lookup requires a UTF-8 path. A working file with a non-UTF-8 name can still be read directly, without a Git diff.

The reader shows the whole file with changed lines marked, and colours the languages below. Working files and files at a commit are recognised the same way, by file name, in any letter case. It uses a small scanner, not a full parser. Other files show as plain text, as does a script whose `#!` line names a different language from its extension. The working-file reader will not open a file outside the project through a linked folder.

### Languages

| Language | Files | Coloured across lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | `.rs` | Nested block comments, strings, raw strings |
| Python | `.py`, `.pyi` | Triple-quoted strings |
| JavaScript, TypeScript | `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx` | Block comments, template strings |
| Go | `.go` | Block comments, raw strings |
| Java | `.java` | Block comments, text blocks |
| Kotlin | `.kt`, `.kts` | Nested block comments, raw strings |
| Scala | `.scala`, `.sc`, `.sbt` | Nested block comments, raw strings |
| Dart | `.dart` | Nested block comments, triple-quoted strings |
| C, C++ | `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hpp`, `.hh` | Block comments, C++ raw strings |
| C# | `.cs` | Block comments, verbatim and raw strings |
| Swift | `.swift` | Nested block comments, multiline and raw strings |
| PHP | `.php` | Block comments, strings, heredocs |
| Ruby | `.rb`, `.rake`, `.gemspec`, `.ru`, `Gemfile`, `Rakefile` | `=begin` comments, heredocs |
| Elixir | `.ex`, `.exs` | Triple-quoted strings |
| Lua | `.lua` | Long comments and long strings |
| Shell | `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh` | Quoted strings |
| SQL | `.sql` | Block comments |
| HTML, SVG, Vue, Svelte | `.html`, `.htm`, `.xhtml`, `.svg`, `.vue`, `.svelte` | Comments, tags, attribute values, and the JavaScript and CSS inside `script` and `style` |
| XML | `.xml` | Comments, tags, attribute values |
| CSS, SCSS, Less | `.css`, `.scss`, `.less` | Block comments |
| Markdown | `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx` | Fenced code blocks, comments |
| JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc` | Block comments |
| YAML | `.yaml`, `.yml` | Quoted strings |
| TOML | `.toml` | Multiline strings |
| Terraform, HCL | `.tf`, `.tfvars`, `.hcl` | Block comments, heredocs |
| Dockerfile | `Dockerfile`, `.dockerfile` | |
| Makefile | `Makefile`, `GNUmakefile`, `.mk` | |

Every language has its comments, strings, numbers and reserved words coloured. Markup has tag names, attributes and entities coloured instead, and text between tags is left plain. Markdown has headings, list marks, links, inline code, code blocks and quotes coloured; emphasis and tables stay plain, and a code block is one colour whatever language it holds. Ruby and Elixir strings in quotes are coloured one line at a time. Colour never changes the text shown, and the marks for added, removed and changed words are drawn over it.

When a removed line and the added line that replaces it look alike, the reader highlights the words that changed. A word is a run of letters, digits and underscores in any script; text written without spaces, such as Chinese or Japanese, is compared one character at a time. Highlighting only adds emphasis: the text shown is the same with or without it. Lines that share too little, lines with many separate changes and lines whose edits span more than about a hundred words keep only their red or green background, as do the remaining lines of an unusually large diff.

The reader also labels hidden differences next to the text: `[tab]` versus `[4 spaces]`, `[LF]` versus `[CRLF]`, or a mark such as `[zero-width space U+200B]`. It highlights the character affected by a changed mark, including a combining accent. Ordinary edits do not label unchanged whitespace or marks. Use the horizontal scroll keys to reach labels on long lines.

Press `n` or `N` to jump to the next or previous change. The Reader briefly shows your position (for example, `Change 2 of 5`) or `No changes` if there is nothing to jump to. Navigation wraps in both directions.

## Editing files

The reader only reads until you ask it to edit. Press `e`, or open the file with `milo view FILE --edit`, and the file's text becomes a draft with a cursor. It works the same in the reader Outline opens in its own pane, in the floating reader in Rex and in `milo view`. The last row lists the main keys, `Ctrl-G` opens help, and [keys and marks](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md#editing-in-the-reader) has the whole list.

The draft is yours alone until you save: the file on disk is not touched by typing, pasting, undoing or formatting. While you edit, the reader shows the draft with its code colours and no change marks. When you stop, it shows the file again at the same lines, with a fresh diff, and Outline still has the file selected.

The editor is for small changes. It has one cursor and no selection or search, and it edits a file that exists: it does not make a new one. The cursor moves one character at a time, so an accent written as a separate mark takes a key press of its own.

### What can be edited

A working file can be edited when it is a regular file, is reached without passing through a link, holds UTF-8 text with no NUL bytes, is no larger than 2 MiB and can be written by you. A byte-order mark is allowed. Anything else stays read-only. The last row then never has `e edit`, and `e` or help says why. A narrow pane can also lack room for `e edit` on a file that can be edited; `e` works all the same.

| It says | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `this is a commit` | The reader shows the file as of a commit, from History or `--commit` |
| `this is a link` | The file is a link; the reader shows where it points |
| `reached through a link` | A folder on the way to the file is a link |
| `the project moved` | The project's folder was renamed or replaced after the reader opened |
| `outside the project` | The path leads out of the project |
| `the file is gone` | The file was removed; the reader may still show its removed lines |
| `not a regular file` | It is a folder, a device or a pipe |
| `not text` | It holds NUL bytes or is not UTF-8, which a save could not keep, or Git treats it as binary |
| `shown as a picture` | The reader is showing it as a picture |
| `it cannot be shown` | The reader shows a note in its place, such as `Too large to show.` |
| `too large` | It is larger than 2 MiB, though the reader can show its changes |
| `no write permission` | You may read it but not write it |
| `it cannot be read` | The file or a folder on the way could not be opened |

A draft cannot grow past 2 MiB either: a key or paste that would take it there is refused.

### Saving

`Ctrl-S` writes the draft into the file that was read. Milo does not put a new file in its place, so the file keeps its permissions, owner, other names and attributes. The bytes you did not edit stay the same: a byte-order mark is kept, every line keeps its own ending when a file mixes `LF` and `CRLF`, and a file with no final line break is not given one. A new line takes the ending most of the file uses.

Before it writes, milo opens the file again and reads it. Nothing is overwritten unexpectedly:

- If the file no longer holds what your edit started from, or another file has been put in its place, nothing is written and the pane asks `Changed on disk: o overwrite · Esc back`. Only `o` writes your draft over it.
- If the file is gone, it is not made again.
- If the file has become a link, or a folder on the way has become a link or moved, the save is refused. Milo never writes through a link.
- If you no longer have permission to write, the save is refused.

In each case the draft stays open, and the last row says what happened. If the write itself fails part of the way, milo puts the old contents back where it can and says whether it could.

A save writes in place, not through a temporary file; that is what keeps the file's links and attributes. A crash or power loss in the middle of a save can therefore leave a partly written file.

### Leaving unsaved changes

`Esc`, `Ctrl-Q` and `Ctrl-C` stop editing. With unsaved changes they ask `Unsaved edits: s save · d discard · Esc back` first. `q` is a letter while you edit. If the terminal has stopped taking output, `Ctrl-C` ends the reader at once, as it always has; the draft is then kept as described next.

A reader can also be ended from outside: its terminal is closed, the process is asked to stop, or Rex closes its pane. If it has unsaved changes, milo writes the draft to the `drafts` folder of its state folder (`~/.local/state/milo`, or `milo` under an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME`), readable only by you, and prints one line about it once the terminal is yours again. The project is not written to. If milo has no state folder, because neither that variable nor `HOME` names one, the line says the edits were lost.

The next time you edit that file, the pane asks `Kept draft found: r restore · d delete · Esc later`. Restoring puts the kept text in place of the file's as one change, so `Ctrl-Z` shows the file as it is now. The kept copy is removed when you delete it or save the restored text, not before: saving other edits, or undoing the restore and then saving or leaving, keeps it. One draft is kept for each file, so a reader that is ended again with unsaved changes to that file replaces it. A process that is killed outright, or a machine that loses power, keeps nothing.

In Rex, opening another file from Outline or History replaces the floating reader. While that reader has unsaved changes, the pane says `The open reader has unsaved edits.` and leaves it alone.

## Formatting

While editing, `Ctrl-F` gives the draft to a formatter and puts its answer in place of the draft as one change. The file is not touched: look the result over, press `Ctrl-Z` to take it back, or discard it with the draft. Only `Ctrl-S` writes it. Keys pressed after `Ctrl-F` wait for the formatter and act on what it answered. If the formatter fails, the draft is left exactly as it was and the last row shows the first line of what the formatter said.

Milo runs a formatter you have installed. It does not install one, download one or run one through a package runner. For each kind of file, the first of these found is used:

| Files | Formatter | Run as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.rs` | rustfmt | `rustfmt --edition E --emit stdout` |
| `.go` | gofmt | `gofmt` |
| `.py`, `.pyi` | ruff, then black | `ruff format --no-cache --stdin-filename ./NAME -`<br>`black --quiet --stdin-filename ./NAME -` |
| `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`, `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.css` | prettier, then biome, then deno | `prettier --stdin-filepath ./NAME`<br>`biome format --stdin-file-path ./NAME`<br>`deno fmt --ext EXT -` |
| `.scss`, `.less`, `.html`, `.md`, `.yaml`, `.yml` | prettier, then deno | As above |
| `.vue` | prettier | As above |
| `.toml` | taplo | `taplo format --stdin-filepath ./NAME -` |
| `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hpp`, `.hh` | clang-format | `clang-format --assume-filename=NAME` |
| `.sh`, `.bash` | shfmt | `shfmt --filename ./NAME` |
| `.lua` | stylua | `stylua --stdin-filepath ./NAME -` |
| `.swift` | swift-format | `swift-format format --assume-filename ./NAME` |
| `.tf`, `.tfvars` | terraform | `terraform fmt -no-color -` |

`NAME` is the file's name and `EXT` its extension. For Rust, `E` is the edition in the nearest `Cargo.toml` at or above the file within the project, or 2021; the option is left out when a `rustfmt.toml` there sets an edition. Other kinds of file, including some the reader colours such as Kotlin, Ruby, Java, C#, PHP and SQL, have no formatter: `Ctrl-F` says `No formatter for this kind of file.` and the last row does not offer it.

How a formatter is run:

- **Only when you press `Ctrl-F`.** Opening, reading and editing a file never start one. Help looks for the program so that it can name it, and does not run it.
- **By name, from where you installed it.** The program is looked for in the folders of `PATH` that are written in full. A folder written relative to where milo runs, such as `.` or `node_modules/.bin`, is skipped, so a project cannot supply the program. The formatter's own `PATH` has those folders taken out too, so a launcher that starts `node` cannot find one in the project. If none is installed, the last row says which to install, for example `Not installed: ruff or black.`
- **On the draft, not the file.** The draft goes in on standard input and the formatted text comes back on standard output. The formatter is not asked to write anything.
- **In the file's folder, with the file's name.** That is how a formatter finds the project's settings, such as `rustfmt.toml`, `pyproject.toml` or `.prettierrc`. Those settings belong to the project, and some formatters load code named in them: Prettier loads plugins and JavaScript settings files. Format files only in a project you trust, as you would in an editor.
- **For at most ten seconds.** After that the formatter and the programs it started are stopped. A formatter that leaves a helper running with its output still open is waited for just as long, and its answer is not used. An answer that is empty, is not UTF-8 text or is larger than 2 MiB is refused.
- **Without downloads.** Milo installs nothing. A `rustfmt` installed by rustup is told not to fetch the toolchain a project's `rust-toolchain.toml` names: if that toolchain is missing, the last row says so.
- **Keeping the file's line endings.** If the file uses `CRLF` and the formatter answers with `LF`, the draft gets `CRLF` back. A byte-order mark is not given to the formatter and is kept.

The pane shows `Formatting with NAME…` and does not redraw until the formatter is done.

## Reading pictures

The working-file reader can show PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, HEIC and HEIF, TIFF, BMP, ICO and ICNS, SVG, PSD and the first page of a PDF, where conversion is supported. It fits the picture without changing its proportions. On macOS, `/usr/bin/sips` converts other formats and resizes large PNGs; other systems show only PNGs that do not need conversion. Ordinary text still shows as text if a file has a picture extension. At a commit, the reader shows the stored file as text or a note, not as a picture.

Pictures need a terminal that supports the kitty graphics protocol, such as Rex. Milo asks the terminal whether it can draw pictures and shows a message if it cannot.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md

# Keys and marks

Press `?` for help when the pane has room. `Esc`, `q` or `?` closes help; `Ctrl-C` quits milo. Text pasted through a terminal that marks pastes is not read as key presses. While you are [editing a file](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md#editing-in-the-reader), the keys you type are text: help is `Ctrl-G`, and `Ctrl-C` asks before it gives up unsaved changes.

## Moving around

These keys work in the outline tree, history and reader. The reader and help page scroll instead of moving a selection.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Up / Down or `k` / `j` | Move one row |
| Page Up / Page Down or `Ctrl-B` / `Ctrl-F` | Move one page |
| `Ctrl-U` / `Ctrl-D` | Move half a page |
| Home / End or `g` / `G` | Go to the first or last row |
| Mouse wheel | Scroll |

### Outline

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Open or close a folder, or read a file |
| `Space` | Open or close a folder |
| Left or `h` | Close an open folder, or go to the parent |
| Right or `l` | Open a closed folder |
| `{` / `}` | Previous or next visible folder |
| `K` / `J` | Previous or next item in the same folder, skipping nested rows |
| `p` | Go to the parent folder |
| `e` | Open every folder; press again to restore your choices |
| `n` / `N` | Jump to the next or previous changed file, including inside closed folders. If there’s nowhere to jump, the tree says why. |
| `c` | Switch between the whole tree and changed files only |
| `r` | Reload |
| `q` | Quit |

Click a folder to open or close it, click a file to select it, or double-click a file to read it. In the short Outline strip, double-click a filename to read it; a single click doesn’t scroll the strip. There’s no keyboard cursor: arrows, `h` / `l`, `j` / `k`, the wheel and Page Up / Page Down scroll one column at a time. Home / End or `g` / `G` go to either end.

### History

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Show or hide a commit's files, show the rest of a long file list, or read the selected file |
| Left or `h` | From a file, return to its commit; from an open commit, close its file list |
| Right or `l` | Open the selected commit's files. In a narrow focused pane, page through a long subject first. |
| `r` | Reload |
| `q` | Quit |

Click a commit to toggle its files, click a file to select it, or double-click to read it as it was at that commit. For a merge, the file list compares the commit with its first parent.

### Reader

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `b` / `Space` | Scroll a page up or down |
| Left / Right or `h` / `l` | Scroll sideways |
| `n` / `N` | Next or previous block of added or removed lines |
| `e` | Edit the file, or say why it is read-only |
| `q` or `Esc` | Close |

The last row shows `e edit` when the file can be edited and the row has room. Help lists the reason when it cannot, and the formatter that would run.

### Editing in the reader

Press `e` in the reader, or start with `milo view FILE --edit`. The heading says `editing`, then `unsaved` once the draft differs from the file. Nothing is written until you save. See [editing files](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#editing-files) for what can be edited and how a save is kept safe.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl-S` | Save the draft to the file |
| `Ctrl-Z` / `Ctrl-Y` | Undo or redo. A run of typing is undone a word at a time |
| `Ctrl-F` | Format the draft with an [installed formatter](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#formatting). `Ctrl-Z` takes it back |
| `Esc`, `Ctrl-Q` or `Ctrl-C` | Stop editing. With unsaved changes, asks: `s` save, `d` discard, `Esc` back |
| Arrows | Move the cursor. Up and Down keep their column through shorter lines |
| Home / End or `Ctrl-A` / `Ctrl-E` | Start or end of the line |
| Page Up / Page Down | Move a page |
| `Enter` | New line, indented like the one above |
| `Tab` | Indent by a tab or by the file's own number of spaces |
| Backspace or `Ctrl-H` | Delete the character before the cursor |
| Delete or `Ctrl-D` | Delete the character under the cursor |
| `Ctrl-G` | Help |
| Click | Put the cursor there |
| Mouse wheel | Scroll without moving the cursor |

Pasted text is inserted as one change, with the file's line endings and without control characters. A paste larger than 1 MiB is refused. Every other key types itself, including `?` and `q`.

Questions take the place of the last row and wait for one of the keys they list. Any other key is ignored. When the pane is two rows tall they take the heading's row instead. A narrow pane drops the words before the keys first: at 28 columns every key is still listed.

| Question | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `Unsaved edits` | `s` save and stop editing, `d` discard the draft, `Esc` go back to it |
| `Changed on disk` | `o` write your draft over the file as it is now, `Esc` go back without writing |
| `Kept draft found` | `r` put the kept draft in place of the text, `d` delete it, `Esc` decide later |

### Usage and setup

In Usage, `r` checks local data without bypassing the [oh-my-pi read interval](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#where-the-figures-come-from), and `q` quits. In setup, use `1`–`4` or `Tab` for Layout, Appearance, Workflow and Health. Up / Down or `k` / `j` selects a row; `Enter` or `Space` activates it. In Layout, `a` tries the current draft and `u` undoes the trial. `s` asks **where** to save; choose the scope and confirm. `Esc` backs out of a confirmation without saving.

## Colours and marks

In a Git outline, **bold** means changes to commit and regular coloured names mean changes to push. Plain names have no changes marked.

If color or font weight is hard to distinguish, enable text change marks in setup. For a still outline while tools write files, choose static activity marks. Neither option changes the terminal's appearance for other programs.

| Colour | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Yellow | Edited |
| Green | Added; italic if Git does not track it yet |
| Red, struck through | Removed |
| Cyan, italic | Moved |
| Magenta | Left in conflict by a merge |

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Pulsing `●` / `○` at the left edge | Being written now |
| `•` at the left edge | Changed since you last looked |
| `docs 3` on a closed folder | Three changed files inside |
| `+7 −5` | Seven lines added and five removed |
| `○5 ↑2` in a narrow outline | Five files to commit and two to push |

When focus is elsewhere, the outline can follow the file being written (for example, `following tides.ts`). It does not move the cursor while you use it or reopen a folder you closed.

Following file activity and following a shell are different choices. File activity moves the outline selection within a project; shell following changes the project shown by an attached pane. Pin a pane's project if you want to keep reading it while the shell moves elsewhere.

In history, a hollow dot means uncommitted work. With a remote branch to compare against, a bold dot marks a commit not on that branch, and a faint dot marks one already on it. A regular dot means there is no comparison. The heading says `no branch tracked` if the current branch does not track a remote branch; that does not mean there are no commits to push. A `•` beside a commit means it arrived while the pane was open. Open a commit to see what changed in each file, in the same colours as the outline.

In the reader, added lines have a green background and keep their code colours; removed lines stay in place with a red background. If only some words of a line changed, those words are highlighted.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md

# Usage limits

`milo usage` shows how much of a reported limit is **left**, not how much has been used. It shows the tools that have something to show, and gives the whole pane to them. The two-row rail gives each of two tools one line for its most constrained window, and a tool on its own both rows. When there's room, it adds the reset countdown for a recent reading or when an older reading was last seen. Wide panes can show large figures and provider marks. Choose large figures in setup if you prefer them in a taller rail too.

A fresh **0% left** means the tool actually reported no remaining capacity. An older reading is marked as historical; once its reset time passes, Milo shows **reset elapsed**, not a fresh percentage. A missing reading is neither zero nor 100%. Run `milo doctor` to see which local source supplied a reading.

## macOS menu bar

With a menu-enabled CLI on macOS 13 or later, run `milo menubar install` to install and open `~/Applications/Milo.app`. Run it again to reopen or upgrade. `milo menubar uninstall` stops the app, unregisters launch at login if enabled, and removes only the app. Neither command needs sudo or a download.

If you have the older `Milo Usage.app`, run the install command again. It migrates the app to `Milo.app`; you don’t need to uninstall first.

You can also manage the menu app from Home (`milo`), under **Workflow** in terminal Settings (`milo setup`), or in the **Menu Bar** tab in web Settings (`milo web`). On current source builds, **Open or update** reopens the installed app or applies the CLI’s bundled update. Removal is a separate, confirmed action. It keeps the Milo CLI, your settings, and any unsaved Settings draft.

The Apple Silicon Homebrew and release binaries include the app starting with v0.1.4. If you prefer to build it from source:

```sh
sh macos/build-menu.sh
./target/local-menu/milo menubar install
```

For a source build, use `./target/local-menu/milo` for subsequent menu commands. On `main`, both build modes omit personal paths. Run `milo menubar install` from the shell whose provider and configuration paths you want the menu to use; run it again if they change. These paths live in a private file beside the installed app, not in the signed bundle. The app has its own reader and does not require Rex.

If the CLI that installed the app has changed or moved, **Browser settings…** opens the bundled editor instead. Run `milo menubar install` from the new CLI to restore menu management from that editor. The published v0.1.4 release predates install-time profile capture and uses default provider paths.

Click the menu bar item to see the same local usage windows as the pane. The menu uses **global** provider visibility, not the preferences of whichever worktree happens to be focused. Automatic display picks the lowest fresh remaining percentage; when none is fresh it shows just Milo. Options lets you pin a provider, show only the mascot, or opt into launch at login. Quitting the app also stops its reader.

Hover over the percentage to see which provider and limit it represents, how much is left, and when it resets if known. Open the menu to see that same window first. Icon-only mode keeps the usual provider order.

Low-quota notifications are **off by default**. In **More options → Low-quota alerts**, choose 10%, 20%, or 30% remaining and allow notifications when macOS asks. Milo alerts only when a visible provider’s fresh reading moves from above your threshold to at or below it, at most once for that provider and reset time. Starting below the threshold is silent. Stale, elapsed, hidden, and unknown-reset readings do not trigger alerts. Choose **Off** to stop them.

![Milo’s native menu with example Codex and Claude limits and the Settings button](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/menu-bar.webp)

Choose **Browser settings…** to open the [local browser editor](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#browser-editor). To change a specific worktree instead, run `milo web` from that project.

## Which tools appear

Milo gives a tool a place once it has a figure, and no place before that. If you use Codex and Claude Code but not OpenCode, the pane has two places and nothing for OpenCode: no label, no dash and no empty row. Each tool has its own choice under **Appearance** in `milo setup` or **Usage** in `milo web`, saved globally or for a worktree like the other pane preferences. Reopen the pane to apply a change.

| Choice | What the pane does |
| --- | --- |
| Auto, the default | Gives the tool a place while it has a figure saved on this Mac: a limit window for Codex or Claude Code, or tokens OpenCode recorded today. Without one the tool takes no room. |
| Always show | Keeps the tool's place even without a reading. Milo says what it knows, such as `no sessions found` or `could not read saved limits`, instead of inventing a percentage. A pane too small for every tool gives its rows to limits first. |
| Hide | Never shows the tool and does not look for it: its folders are not walked or watched, and its database is not opened. With Codex and Claude Code both hidden, oh-my-pi's database is not opened either. |

Whether a tool is in use here is read from files the tool itself saved. Milo does not run the tool, read its sign-in or use the network to find out.

| Tool | Found when |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | A session file `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` has something in it, or oh-my-pi has saved a Codex report. |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json` has something in it, or a session written today is under `~/.claude/projects`, or the status line or oh-my-pi has saved a limit report. |
| OpenCode | The file where it keeps its database is a SQLite database. |

Empty folders, empty files, another kind of file under the same name and a Claude Code directory that holds only settings do not count. Links to individual sources or within the session trees are not followed. A report oh-my-pi saved for a tool does count, even when nothing else of the tool is on disk. The looks are the bounded reads described under [Where the figures come from](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#where-the-figures-come-from).

Milo uses `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` instead of `~/.codex/sessions` when Codex has an explicit home. With `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, it looks for `.claude.json`, `projects/` and `settings.json` inside that directory, not in the default profile. Run Milo and Claude Code with the same override to see and configure that profile's usage.

A tool that is found but has no figure yet stays out of the way of the tools that have one. When no tool has a figure, the pane shows one quiet block instead of empty places: what each found tool is waiting for, such as `Claude · no saved limits found` and `Run milo setup`, or `No usage to show yet` and the tools Milo looks for when it found none.

The frame closes up around what is shown:

- **Two tools with limits** share the pane: side by side when it is wide, one above the other on a rail.
- **One tool with limits** has the pane to itself. A rail lists its other windows under the tightest one, and a wide pane keeps its windows together at the left.
- **OpenCode with one of them** takes the second place: the other half of a wide pane, or the lower half of a rail.
- **OpenCode with both** has one row beneath them, from the third row of a rail or in a wide pane at least nine rows tall. Two rows go to the two limits.
- **OpenCode alone** fills the two-row rail with today's tokens, then its cost and steps. A larger pane draws the tokens large.

`milo doctor` follows the same rule. It reports a tool that was found or is always shown, and says nothing of one that is absent or hidden beyond the choice itself.

## Where the figures come from

| Source | What milo reads |
| --- | --- |
| oh-my-pi | Limits the harness saves for Codex and Claude in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` (or `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/agent.db`). Milo reads only the usage data, using `/usr/bin/sqlite3` in read-only mode. Automatic reads are at least 20 seconds apart per pane. |
| Codex | Limit reports in recent Codex session files under `~/.codex/sessions` |
| Claude Code | Its own saved limits in `~/.claude.json`, or limits sent through the status line if you turn it on in setup. |
| OpenCode | Today's activity, not limits, from its session database. See [OpenCode activity](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#opencode-activity). |

For each tool, milo uses the newest report it can read. When there is room, it also shows **tokens today** from Claude Code's local session files under `~/.claude/projects`. This is local activity since midnight, not a limit. It counts new input, output and cache writes, not cache reads. A `+` after the number means the total may be incomplete.

A report dated more than five minutes ahead of this machine's clock is not used, whichever source it came from. Otherwise one report written while a clock was wrong would outrank every later one. Milo shows the newest of the remaining sources instead. A deferred Codex or Claude Code report becomes eligible as the clock catches up, even if the source file has not changed. For the status-line save, the next report from Claude Code replaces the misdated file.

Milo checks the tails of recent Codex logs, then resumes near the previous end as those logs grow. Ordinary session activity does not clear the last limit report. A new or replaced log, a truncation, or a large burst of new data calls for another bounded tail check.

While a Codex log has been active in the last five minutes, Milo checks known logs about every two seconds, even if the writer keeps the file open. With a native watcher, Milo groups notifications so it doesn’t walk the session directories on every write. Without a watcher, it looks for new Codex and Claude Code sessions on the roughly two-second fallback checks. Press `r` to check immediately.

Milo labels reports as older after five minutes, or ten minutes for oh-my-pi to allow for its provider refresh cadence. This uses the time the provider's window was last observed, not the time Milo read the file.

**Show Claude Code limits** in `milo setup` adds a status line if you do not already have one. Claude Code calls `milo claude-status` to show a short line and save the reported limits to `~/.local/state/milo/claude-limits.json` (or under an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). It does not save prompts or replies. You do not need to enable it if Claude Code or oh-my-pi already saves a report.
Each explicit `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` has its own `claude-limits.json` under Milo's `claude-profiles/` state directory, so a reading from another profile is not used as a fallback.

An unchanged status-line reading confirms the same window, but Milo saves that confirmation at most once a minute per window. A lower figure for the same window or an older reset does not replace or refresh the saved figure.
If an update leaves out the reset time, it can update a nondecreasing figure without discarding the last known reset.

## OpenCode activity

OpenCode saves no limits on this machine, so Milo shows none for it. What it does save is each step's token counts and its own cost estimate. Beneath two tools with limits Milo gives it one line, such as `OpenCode · 48.2k tokens today · $1.37 est.`. A narrower pane drops the cost first, then shortens the rest. Beside one tool, or alone, it also shows the number of steps, when the last one was recorded and the cache reads. [Which tools appear](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#which-tools-appear) says where it goes at each size.

| Figure | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Tokens today | New input, output, reasoning and cache writes of the assistant steps OpenCode recorded since local midnight, in every project. Cache reads are left out, as they are for Claude Code. It is activity, not a share of any limit. |
| Cost | The sum OpenCode recorded for those steps, in US dollars. It is OpenCode's estimate from model prices, not a bill: a subscription or an unpriced model records zero, and Milo shows nothing rather than `$0`. A `+` means some steps recorded no cost. |
| Limits | Unknown. OpenCode asks its own servers for allowances and budgets when you open them, and does not save the answer. Milo does not ask and does not use OpenCode's saved sign-in. |

Milo reads `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, or the same file under an absolute `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, or the file `$OPENCODE_DB` names. It uses `/usr/bin/sqlite3` in read-only mode for at most a second, at least 20 seconds apart. The queries return sums and times only: message text never leaves the database, and the tables that hold OpenCode's sign-in are not read. The line can lag OpenCode by about half a minute; press `r` to read now.

The figures were checked against databases written by OpenCode 1.2.0, 1.19.6, 2.2.0 and 2.3.2. They match `opencode stats --days 0`, except that Milo does not count a forked session's copied steps again on the day OpenCode 1 is upgraded to 2. Milo shows nothing, and `milo doctor` reports OpenCode's activity as unknown, when the database has other tables, when a step from today is malformed, when one of today's sessions was created by a version other than 1.x or 2.x, or when OpenCode 1 is still writing to a database OpenCode 2 has upgraded. Title requests are not counted, nor are OpenCode 2's compaction requests, because OpenCode does not record them as steps. [Usage sources](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage-sources.md) has the evidence, the limits of this reading, and why Amp and Gemini CLI are not read.

## Accounts asked online

Some figures exist only on a provider's servers. Milo can ask for four of them, and asks for none until you turn that account on. Each is hidden by default: with the choice left at **Hide**, Milo does not read the key, does not contact the provider and shows nothing, whatever keys are in your environment.
